item.title: SpaceX renames Superintelligence division to Artificial Intelligence amid midterm spending reports
item.description:
SpaceX renames Superintelligence division to Artificial Intelligence amid midterm spending reports

SpaceX has transitioned the name of its “Superintelligence” division back to “Artificial Intelligence.” This administrative change occurs as reports detail that Elon Musk spent nearly $500 million on midterm elections, including significant financial involvement in Texas state politics.

⚙️ Key details

  • The internal division previously known as “Superintelligence” at SpaceX has been renamed to “Artificial Intelligence.”
  • This change in nomenclature was described as being free to implement.
  • Simultaneously, Elon Musk was observed deleting social media posts following the conclusion of election cycles.

🔍 Overview

Elon Musk directed nearly $500 million toward midterm elections. A specific portion of this funding, totaling $47 million from America PAC, was used in an effort to defeat Texas Democrat James Talarico. Talarico won the election with 55 percent of the vote against Musk’s preferred candidate, Ken Paxton. In his campaign, Talarico utilized the slogan “Texas is not for sale” to highlight Musk’s financial influence.

📊 Comparative valuation

The $500 million spent on election efforts represents a sum that could have acquired various high-value assets or infrastructure projects:

Item Estimated Quantity or Value
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards 223,000 units at MSRP or 60,000 units at globalized normal price
Larry Ellison’s private island $440 million (adjusted for inflation)
Willem de Kooning’s Interchange ~$400 million (adjusted for inflation)
The Washington Post $360 million (adjusted for inflation)
Ken Griffin’s NYC penthouse $321 million (adjusted for inflation)
Blue Origin’s New Shepard rides At least 977 rides
Super Bowl commercials 44 30-second spots
Gift cards for Texans $14.67 for every resident (approx. 30 million people)
Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool renovations 34 total renovations

💡 Why it matters

The outcome of these elections has brought a wave of politicians into power who campaigned against Musk’s financial influence, including the governor and the attorney general of Texas. This shift in leadership has led to increased scrutiny regarding “sweetheart deals” intended to benefit Musk. Potential transparency measures may include the unredacting of official emails from Gov. Greg Abbott to clarify the extent of the influence purchased through political contributions.

Source: 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million

item.title: Texas AI Data Center Boom Meets New Political and Regulatory Hurdles
item.description:
Texas AI Data Center Boom Meets New Political and Regulatory Hurdles

Texas has become the new epicenter of the AI data‑center build‑out, but recent election results and a governor‑directed permit halt are reshaping the landscape.

🔍 Overview

  • Texas is the fastest‑growing data‑center market in the U.S. and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI build‑outs.
  • Some of the world’s largest AI infrastructure projects are under construction in the state.
  • Until September, Texas was considered the easiest place to build data centers.

🗳️ Political Shift

  • Democrat James Talarico won the U.S. Senate seat against Ken Paxton.
  • Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against incumbent Greg Abbott.
  • Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years.
  • Both Talarico and Hinojosa made data‑center issues central to their campaigns, discussing them constantly on the trail.
  • Voters supported measures to protect ratepayers from electricity‑bill increases caused by data centers and favored broader bans on new data centers.
  • County‑level voting patterns show mixed support: Dallas County and nearby areas voted blue, while Ellis County (a leading permit‑request county) voted red; Cameron County, a data‑center hot spot, shifted blue, whereas Mitchell and Scurry Counties, home to western projects, voted red.

🏗️ Major Projects

Project Planned Capacity (MW) Primary Purpose
Stargate Frontier (Shackelford County) 1,820 General AI infrastructure (comparable to SpaceX’s Colossus 2)
Nexus Hubbard (under construction) 6,400 Intended mostly to serve Anthropic; second‑largest U.S. data center behind Meta’s Hyperion

📉 Industry Reaction

  • At the DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, panelists lamented the September 21 directive from Governor Abbott that halted data‑center permits.
  • Panelists expected the halt to potentially slow existing projects and halt new ones altogether.
  • Banks and lenders are already becoming pickier about financing these projects.
  • Local officials who have some say over development may resist sweeping state restrictions, because no single office decides a project’s fate.

🔮 Outlook

  • The combination of a newly Democratic‑controlled legislature, a governor‑directed permit freeze, and voter concerns about electricity costs creates uncertainty for Texas’ AI data‑center pipeline.
  • Industry participants are watching both state regulatory actions and local political dynamics as they determine the future pace of construction.

#AIDataCenters #TexasPolitics #Infrastructure

Source: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
